feature_api.input: One device, chronological numeric rows. No labels, device IDs or future rows. Select literal column names from profile.feature_names.
feature_api.output: pd.DataFrame of declared unique fe_ columns; preserve rows and index. Original columns are retained automatically.

past_helpers.past.gap_seconds(frame): Series: current minus previous observation time in seconds; first value NaN.
past_helpers.past.observation_count(frame): Series: causal count 1,2,...,n; no measured-value missingness dependence.

rules: Only assignments to new local names and a final return. No loops, comprehensions, imports or arbitrary functions.
frame.index is permitted ONLY as index=frame.index in pd.DataFrame. For time gaps use past.gap_seconds(frame).
No frame.columns, to_series, dt, iloc, loc, values, pd.Series, pd.to_numeric or apply. Inputs are already numeric.
Use arithmetic operators / + - * instead of .div/.add/.sub/.mul. Use literal column names; never discover columns dynamically.
Reductions must directly follow rolling/expanding/ewm. Use trailing real-time rolling windows; center=True and negative shifts are forbidden.
Missing measurements stay unknown unless the hypothesis explicitly justifies a constant or forward fill. No infinities.
Zero finite values in a bounded sample is a coverage limitation, not evidence that the entire dataset is empty.

hypotheses.mechanism: Cumulative correctable-error burden: repeated CEs mark marginal cells/wordlines, so higher past CE volume and larger physical footprint predict impending uncorrectable fault.
hypotheses.basis: DRAM field studies often observe CE storms before UE; repeated errors indicate weak cells.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Failing and healthy devices show overlapping distributions for raw_life_events, raw_life_distinct_cells and raw_24h_events; no positive association.

hypotheses.mechanism: Recent expansion of fault footprint: new rows, columns, and error-bit patterns in the last 7 days indicate accelerating degradation rather than a stable single-cell defect.
hypotheses.basis: Spatially spreading faults suggest growing row/column or bank damage.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Failing devices do not show elevated recent new rows/columns/patterns or 7-day CE activity compared with healthy devices.

hypotheses.mechanism: Multi-bit error severity: CEs with more error bits consume more ECC correction margin and signal stronger cell interference or partial wordline failure.
hypotheses.basis: Higher bit multiplicity reduces ECC margin and reflects broader electrical damage.
hypotheses.falsified_if: No positive difference in maximum error bits per CE between failing and healthy devices.

hypotheses.mechanism: Multi-DQ/symbol extent: CEs spanning multiple DQ lanes indicate I/O or datapath damage, with more DQ lanes per event reflecting a wider electrical fault.
hypotheses.basis: DRAM I/O and datapath failures often produce correlated errors across multiple DQ lanes.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Multi-DQ event counts and max DQ counts are not elevated in failing devices.

hypotheses.mechanism: Risky bitmap shape: error bitmaps not confined to one half of the 8x4 array are harder to correct and may indicate multiple adjacent cells or row/column defects.
hypotheses.basis: Bitmaps crossing the coarse correctability region imply more complex failure geometry.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Risky bitmap event counts do not separate failing from healthy devices.

hypotheses.mechanism: Adjacent-DQ and multi-beat coupling: fatal faults may show either tight adjacency in DQ lanes or broad beat involvement, reflecting crosstalk or timing marginality.
hypotheses.basis: I/O crosstalk and rank/bank timing marginality can create correlated symbol and beat errors.
hypotheses.falsified_if: No joint difference in adjacent-DQ, minimum DQ interval, multi-beat or max-beat statistics between failing and healthy groups.

hypotheses.mechanism: Hot-cell concentration versus broad dispersion: a dominant hot cell may repeat without progressing, while broad row/column spread indicates systemic degradation.
hypotheses.basis: Different DRAM failure modes produce either concentrated single-cell signatures or widespread row/column damage.
hypotheses.falsified_if: These concentration/dispersion summaries show no separation between failing and healthy devices.

hypotheses.mechanism: Patrol scrub detection share: a higher share of CEs found by patrol scrub indicates latent defects not triggered only by demand traffic.
hypotheses.basis: Background scrub reads can reveal weak cells before demand accesses encounter them.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Patrol scrub share is not elevated in failing devices.

hypotheses.mechanism: Short-horizon burstiness and temporal clustering: bursts within one hour and high event frequency indicate unstable cells or transient voltage/temperature margin loss.
hypotheses.basis: CE bursts often reflect repeated accesses to marginal cells or unstable operating conditions.
hypotheses.falsified_if: No temporal clustering signal in 1-hour storm/burst/interval/frequency metrics differs between failing and healthy devices.

hypotheses.mechanism: Fault mode localization at bank/device level: high counts of bank- or device-level fault modes represent broader control/address damage than isolated cell faults.
hypotheses.basis: Bank and device fault modes imply larger physical or logical units are affected.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Bank- or device-level fault mode counts are not higher in failing devices.

hypotheses.mechanism: Rapid onset from first CE: devices that fail shortly after their first observed CE have acute defects, while long stable histories with old CEs are less dangerous.
hypotheses.basis: Short time from first CE to failure suggests rapid progression of an acute fault.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Failing devices do not show shorter days since first CE than healthy devices.

acceptance_rule.explanation: best changes only when paired CV bootstrap P(better) >= 0.9 and CV F1 gain > lower_bound
